title: Fleet capacity override playbook + throughput snapshot UI
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: Implement a Fleet Controls Console surface that exposes capacity override controls, a compact throughput snapshot (real-time + historical), and an immutable change history export. Goal is to let operators rapidly apply temporary capacity overrides (eg. emergency scaling margins), inspect short-term throughput and latency trends, and audit who changed fleet targets and why.

Motivation: Customers on Dedicated want a fast path to apply short-lived capacity adjustments without changing policy code or performing a full rollout. Current console surfaces show scaling presets and long-term audit logs but lack a concise "override+snapshot" workflow for incident response and SRE runbooks. This ticket scopes the PM requirements, acceptance criteria, and cross-team handoffs for the UI, API contract, and telemetry.

Scope:
- New "Overrides" panel in Fleet Controls: create/edit temporary capacity overrides (duration, CPU/GPU reserve, target throughput, optional note) with soft/fail-safe validation.
- Throughput Snapshot widget: 1/5/15/60 minute windows; shows p95 latency, tokens/sec, queued requests, and effective concurrency. Includes small-sparkline and ability to expand to the existing throughput dashboard.
- Change History export: present an immutable timeline of overrides and scaling policy changes with user, timestamp, reason, and linked PR or runbook. Export as CSV and include server-side signed URL for downloads.
- API contract: expose endpoints for create/list/delete overrides and for fetching snapshot metrics; engineering to provide schema.
- Guardrails: prevent overlapping conflicting overrides; warn on revisions that reduce guaranteed capacity below SLA threshold.

Out of scope: autoscaling policy rework, billing changes, dedicated-runtime kernel adjustments. Those are separate engineering efforts.

Acceptance criteria:
- PM-designed UI mocks signed off by Design and Eng.
- API endpoints implemented and documented in the Console API spec.
- Override lifecycle: can create an override with duration up to 72 hours, system enforces non-overlap and shows conflicts.
- Snapshot provides <10s stale metrics and matches backend telemetry on spot checks.
- Change history shows entries for overrides and policy rollouts for the last 90 days and CSV exports include all displayed columns.
- E2E QA checklist and runbook updated for incident scenarios using overrides.

2025-02-14 - Lucas Zhang: Met with Design (Marina) and Eng (Ravi) to validate feasibility. Key engineering concerns: race conditions between autoscaler and override engine, and telemetry sampling for 1-minute buckets. Ravi suggests a TTL-based override object and lease check at the autoscaler entrance. Logged ENG-28901 as dependency.

2025-02-20 - Marina Lee (Design): Uploaded 3 variants of the Overrides panel (compact, modal, and drawer). PM prefers compact inline panel with emphasis on reason field. Designer requests copy for validation and success/error states. https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/overrides/variants

2025-02-25 - Aisha Kumar: Updated acceptance criteria to include CSV export and signed download URL per legal guidance. Added guardrail: block any override that will drop guaranteed throughput below SLA floor. Need Eng sign-off on enforcement point in pipeline (admission vs actuator).

2025-02-28 - Ravi Patel (Eng): Prototype ready for backend: override API (POST /fleets/:id/overrides), list, delete. Snapshot endpoint will reuse existing telemetry query with a 10s cache TTL. Raised a follow-up ENG ticket to add a conflict detector hook at admission.

2025-03-03 - QA (Natasha Gomez): Draft E2E tests: create override, confirm autoscaler respects override, snapshot reflects tokens/sec change, delete override and confirm reversion. Noted a flaky timing window in staging when autoscaler polls every 12s; suggest reducing poll jitter for tests.

2025-03-05 - Aisha Kumar: Wireframes approved by PM/Design. Blocker cleared after Eng confirmed conflict detector will return human-readable error codes. Next: finalize API swagger and schedule a 2-week sprint with Eng to deliver MVP.
